study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter natural history cohort study
outcome: Need for specific surgery types (otolaryngology, brain, foramen magnum, spine, and extremity)
cohort: 857 patients with achondroplasia with known route of delivery and maternal stature
finding: In patients with achondroplasia, the route of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) does not affect the odds of requiring postnatal achondroplasia-related surgery.
mod_finding: There was no difference in the odds of requiring any postnatal achondroplasia-related surgery when comparing vaginal delivery to cesarean delivery.
